items.text: Peter Gabriel's "Sledgehammer" reached number one on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1986, his first number one.
items.question: Where were you living when "Sledgehammer" was on the radio, and do you remember seeing its video?
source_quote: The Billboard Hot 100 is a chart published since August 1958 by Billboard magazine which ranks the best-performing singles in the United States. In 1986, it was compiled based on a combination of sales and airplay data sourced from surveys of retail outlets and playlists submitted by radio stations, respectively. During the year, 31 different singles spent time at number one.
After a single week in the top spot, the single was displaced by "Sledgehammer", the first number one for Peter Gabriel

items.text: The Space Shuttle Challenger was lost shortly after launch on January 28, 1986.
items.question: Where were you when you heard about the Challenger, and who told you?
source_quote: STS-51-L: Space Shuttle Challenger disintegrates 73 seconds after launch, killing the crew of seven astronauts, including schoolteacher Christa McAuliffe (see Space Shuttle Challenger disaster).

items.text: The New York Mets beat the Boston Red Sox in seven games to win the 1986 World Series.
items.question: Who did you watch the 1986 World Series with, and were you pulling for the Mets or the Red Sox?
items.source_quote: World Series: The New York Mets defeat the Boston Red Sox in 7 games. This is the second world series title in the Mets franchise. It is also remembered for Game 6, when Bill Buckner lets an easy ground ball hit by Mookie Wilson roll through his legs, letting the Mets win and pull even with the Red Sox in the series.
